artifact.title: An intended order pipeline
artifact.subtitle: A design with no repository behind it
artifact.summary: There is no code for any of this and no repository to point at, so this specification declares no source and carries no citation. That is a legal and complete artifact: the diagram describes something intended rather than something that runs, and the engine reports its evidence layer as not run rather than as passed.

groups.label: At the edge
groups.summary: What a customer would touch. Intended, not built.

nodes.label: Customer
nodes.summary: Places an order and expects one confirmation, not three.

nodes.label: Storefront
nodes.summary: Would accept the order and hand it on without holding it.

nodes.label: Order service
nodes.summary: Would own the order's lifecycle and nothing else.

nodes.label: Order ledger
nodes.summary: Would be the only writer of order state.

nodes.label: order-events
nodes.summary: Would carry what happened, never what should happen next.

nodes.label: Payments
nodes.summary: A third party. Would be called once, idempotently.

nodes.label: Fulfilment
nodes.summary: Would consume events rather than being called.

nodes.label: Retry
nodes.summary: Would decide whether a failed charge is worth another attempt.

paths.label: The intended happy path
paths.note: Three steps, and the order is durable in the ledger before anybody is charged.

paths.label: Charging, and failing
paths.note: The walk returns to the payment provider it just left, which is a cycle and a fact about retries rather than a modelling slip.

views.label: What would be asynchronous
views.note: Fulfilment would never be called directly, which is the whole point of the queue.
